sections.title: Part Ⅰ TASK A. Readback and Hearback

body.label: Ground
body.text: HL123, cross runway two seven, report vacated.
ZORIN

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, after passing ZORIN, descend to flight level one niner zero, reduce speed two five zero knots.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, climb to one five thousand feet, expedite until passing one two thousand.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, cleared for the ILS runway one four approach, maintain one six zero knots to the marker.

sections.title: Part Ⅰ TASK B. Checking, Clarifying, Confirming, Informing

body.text: Approach cleared you to descend maintaining your own visual separation from an Airbus A340 ahead. The A340 has just entered cloud and you no longer have it in sight. Listen to the controller, respond accordingly with a reason, and make a request.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, confirm maintaining visual separation with the Airbus A340?
You are heavy today. The slowest speed you can hold with the flaps you have out is two one zero knots. Listen to the controller, respond with a reason, and tell him what you can do.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, maintain one eight zero knots until four miles. Can you do that?
Hartwell Control

During pushback you saw a ground vehicle drive away leaving a spill of fuel on the apron beside stand one two. You were busy with the checklist and did not report it. Ground now calls you. Listen to the ground, give a full readback, and report what you saw.

body.label: Ground
body.text: HL123, taxi to holding point Charlie via Alpha and Delta.

You are presently established on a heading of two seven zero. The controller's instruction would mean a full turn through three six zero degrees, so you think he may have meant a different heading. Listen to the controller and make a confirmation.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, turn left heading two seven zero.

You were cleared to climb to eight thousand feet, but you set six thousand by mistake and you are now level at six thousand. You want your climb back. Listen to the controller, correct your mistake, and make a request.

body.label: Departure
body.text: HL123, report passing seven thousand.

sections.title: Part Ⅱ TASK A. Role-play & Follow-up

pre.text: Flight Paths In this scenario, you'll be the pilot flying Hotel Lima 123, which goes through three flight stages. Descent, approach, and taxi.

Initial Situation You are the pilot of HL123, descending through flight level two zero zero for one one thousand, 60 miles from TREBO, inbound to Thatcham Airport. You have information Delta. Your required landing distance today is 1,750 metres.

body.text: Contact Thatcham Approach and report your position and level.
TREBO ONE arrival
Listen to the controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, Thatcham Approach, descend to 9,000 feet, reduce speed to two five zero knots, expect the TREBO ONE arrival, ILS runway two seven, Thatcham altimeter two niner eight six.
Listen to the controller, give a full readback, and inquire about the landing distance available.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, descend to 5,000 feet. Be advised there's work in progress on runway two seven — they've displaced the threshold, so you won't have the full length today.
runway two seven / runway two one / landing distance available
Listen to the controller, state your decision with a reason, and tell him the figure you need.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, two seven gives you 1,900 metres from the displaced threshold. Two one has the full 2,600, but you'd be number three behind an Airbus A340 — about one two minutes. Your call.

pre.text: Situation Update You are now established on the TREBO ONE arrival, descending through 7,000 feet.

body.text: Listen to the controller, give a full readback, and inquire how long it will take.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, the Embraer 175 ahead of you has gone around. Turn left heading one eight zero, descend to 4,000 feet, I'll have to slot you back in behind him.
Listen to the controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, turn right heading two four zero, descend to 3,000 feet until established, cleared for the ILS runway two seven approach, contact Thatcham Tower on 118.3.
Listen to the tower and give a full readback.

body.label: Tower
body.text: HL123, Thatcham Tower, runway two seven, cleared to land, wind two five zero at eight, caution work in progress right of the threshold.
Listen to the tower and provide both pieces of information.

body.label: Tower
body.text: HL123, I'm filing a report on the work in progress — say again the landing distance you need, and tell me whether 1,900 metres was enough for you.

pre.text: Situation Update You have landed and vacated runway two seven. You are now stopped on taxiway Kilo, short of taxiway Juliet.

body.text: Stand one two / Stand two zero
Listen to the ground controller, state your decision with a reason, and inquire how long it will take.

body.label: Ground
body.text: HL123, Thatcham Ground, stand one two is still occupied by the Airbus A340 with a technical. I can give you stand two zero, but it's eight minutes of taxi. Or you hold for one two. What would you prefer?
Listen to the ground controller, respond accordingly, and report your position.

body.label: Ground
body.text: HL123, I've lost sight of you behind the hangar — whereabouts are you now?
Follow up question.

In this situation, the runway you were offered had less landing distance than usual because of work in progress. What did you compare before you accepted it, and why? In your role as a pilot, how do you prepare for a runway that turns out shorter than you planned for — on the day, and in your briefing beforehand? Give an example of a figure you have had to re-check because something changed at short notice.

sections.title: Part Ⅱ TASK B. Extended Role-play : Single Incident/Emergency Related

pre.text: Initial Situation You are the pilot of HL123, climbing through 9,000 feet for flight level three one zero, 25 miles south of Stapleton Airport. Your fuel endurance is one hour five zero minutes and there are one four seven persons on board. Your required landing distance is 2,200 metres.

body.text: Contact Stapleton Departure and report your passing altitude.
Listen to the controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Departure
body.text: HL123, Stapleton Departure, climb to flight level three one zero, turn right heading one two zero, contact Hartwell Control on 132.4 when passing one eight thousand.

pre.text: Situation Update Passing one three thousand feet, the cabin crew report smoke coming from the rear galley. You have isolated the galley power but the smoke has not cleared. There is no fire indication on the flight deck.

body.text: Declare an emergency, report the nature of your problem, and request an immediate return.
Listen to the controller and provide the requested information.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, Stapleton Approach, roger your MAYDAY, radar contact. Say your fuel endurance and the number of persons on board.
Stapleton / Brindle / landing distance available
Listen to the controller, state your decision with a reason, and tell him the figure you need.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, Stapleton runway zero niner has 2,400 metres, but with the departure sequence you'd be one five minutes to touchdown. Brindle is niner minutes away with 3,000 metres. What would you like?
Listen to the controller, give a full readback and say your intentions.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, roger, turn left heading two seven zero, descend to 8,000 feet, vectors for Brindle. Say your intentions.
Listen to the controller and answer both of his questions.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, two things for Brindle — is the smoke still in the cabin, and do you want the fire service to meet you on the runway?
Listen to the controller and provide both pieces of information.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, Brindle wants it for the emergency brief — say again your fuel endurance, and say again how many persons on board.

pre.text: Situation Update The smoke has stopped and the cabin is clear. The cabin crew report the galley oven as the source and it is now isolated.

body.text: Listen to the controller, give him an update, state your decision with a reason, and say what you will need on the runway.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, if the cabin's clear now, do you want to cancel the emergency, or keep it in?
Listen to the controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, turn right heading three five zero, descend to 2,500 feet until established, cleared for the ILS runway one four approach, contact Brindle Tower on 119.1.

body.text: What happened to your aircraft (HL123)? Explain the nature of the incident.
How do you think the incident was handled by the air traffic controller? Do you feel the situation could have been handled differently? Make a comment from a pilot's point of view.
